registers.name: CONTROL
registers.description: Control register. Bit 0 stores ENABLE. Bit 1 is SAMPLE_START write-one pulse and reads back as 0. Bit 2 stores IRQ_ENABLE. Bit 3 is ALERT_CLEAR write-one pulse and reads back as 0. Reserved upper bits read as 0 and ignore writes.

fields.name: SAMPLE_START
fields.description: Write 1 to request one conversion. This bit does not store state and always reads as 0.

fields.name: ALERT_CLEAR
fields.description: Write 1 to clear alert_status and STATUS.alert_pending. This bit does not store state and always reads as 0.

registers.name: STATUS
registers.description: Status register. Bit 0 is sticky sample_done. Bit 1 is sticky alert_pending. Bit 2 is sticky adc_valid_seen. Bit 3 is busy while a requested sample is pending. Upper bits read as 0.

fields.name: sample_done
fields.description: Sticky after any completed adc_valid sample until cleared by IRQ_CLEAR bit 1.

fields.name: alert_pending
fields.description: Mirrors latched alert_status until ALERT_CLEAR or IRQ_CLEAR bit 0 is written.

fields.name: adc_valid_seen
fields.description: Sticky after the first adc_valid sample until reset.

fields.name: busy
fields.description: High while a requested sample is pending.

registers.name: THRESHOLD
registers.description: Threshold register. threshold_code is stored in bits [11:0]. Upper bits read as zero.

registers.name: LATEST_TEMP
registers.description: Latest filtered temperature code. temp_code/latest_temp are reported in bits [11:0]. Upper bits read as zero.

fields.name: sample_count
fields.description: Counts completed adc_valid samples. Increments exactly once per completed sample.

registers.name: IRQ_STATUS
registers.description: Sticky interrupt status register. Bit 0 is alert and bit 1 is sample_done. Upper bits read as 0.

fields.name: alert
fields.description: Sticky interrupt status for alert threshold exceed.

fields.name: sample_done
fields.description: Sticky interrupt status for completed sample.

registers.name: IRQ_CLEAR
registers.description: Write-one-to-clear register. Bit 0 clears IRQ_STATUS.alert and alert_status. Bit 1 clears IRQ_STATUS.sample_done and STATUS.sample_done. Readback is zero.

sources.name: ALERT_IRQ
sources.description: Top-level alert_irq output asserted when CONTROL.IRQ_ENABLE is set and either IRQ_STATUS.alert or IRQ_STATUS.sample_done is latched.

sources.name: SAMPLE_DONE
sources.description: Sticky sample completion status reflected in STATUS.sample_done and IRQ_STATUS.sample_done. Not a separate top-level interrupt pin, but contributes to alert_irq when IRQ enabled.

sources.name: ALERT
sources.description: Sticky alert threshold-exceed status reflected in alert_status, STATUS.alert_pending, and IRQ_STATUS.alert. Not a separate top-level interrupt pin, but contributes to alert_irq when IRQ enabled.

init_sequence: Write CONTROL.ENABLE=0 and CONTROL.IRQ_ENABLE=0 if needed for a known baseline.
Program THRESHOLD.threshold_code with the desired 12-bit threshold.
Clear pending sticky state by writing IRQ_CLEAR bit 0 and bit 1 as needed; optionally write CONTROL.ALERT_CLEAR=1 to clear alert_pending/alert_status.
Set CONTROL.ENABLE=1 to allow periodic sampling.
Optionally write CONTROL.SAMPLE_START=1 to request an immediate conversion.
Optionally set CONTROL.IRQ_ENABLE=1 to allow alert_irq assertion.
polling_sequence: Poll STATUS.busy to see whether a requested sample is still pending.
Poll STATUS.sample_done or IRQ_STATUS.sample_done to detect completed samples.
Read LATEST_TEMP to obtain the latest filtered temperature code.
Read SAMPLE_COUNT to track completed conversions.
Read STATUS.alert_pending or IRQ_STATUS.alert to determine whether the threshold was exceeded.
irq_sequence: On alert_irq assertion, read IRQ_STATUS to determine whether alert and/or sample_done caused the interrupt.
If IRQ_STATUS.alert is set, write IRQ_CLEAR bit 0=1 to clear alert IRQ state and alert_status.
If IRQ_STATUS.sample_done is set, write IRQ_CLEAR bit 1=1 to clear sample_done IRQ state and STATUS.sample_done.
Re-arm or continue sampling as required by firmware policy.

consistency_notes: The register map is compatible with DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON and preserves the specified offsets, access types, reset behavior, and sticky/pulse semantics.
No additional hierarchy, ports, bus protocol, or memory-mapped locations were invented beyond the specified abstract 16-bit register interface.
Upper bits not explicitly assigned in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON are represented as zero on readback and ignored on write.
Explicit internal state names requested by the spec remain architecturally visible through the listed registers and sticky status fields.
